name: FOLFOX-6 (Tournigand)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
source.nccnTemplate: pending - per-disease NCCN Chemotherapy Order Template not yet provided

institution.provenance: textbook-grounded draft; NCCN per-disease template + clinical (StewardMD) + hospital/institutional approval pending

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: give before oxaliplatin per moderate emetic risk tier (appendix D)

supportiveCare: Antiemetics: moderate emetic risk tier (oxaliplatin is a moderate-emetic-risk IV agent, 5-FU is low risk; highest-risk-day-of-therapy rule per NCCN appendix D assigns the regimen to the moderate tier) - prophylaxis on day of treatment per NCCN Antiemesis guideline

G-CSF: not routinely indicated - FOLFOX-6 is not listed among NCCN high or intermediate febrile-neutropenia-risk regimens (appendix C); base use on patient-specific risk factors per physician-patient discussion
monitoring: CBC with differential before each cycle
Renal function (creatinine clearance) before each cycle - platinum agent
Baseline and periodic neuropathy assessment (oxaliplatin peripheral neuropathy is cumulative)

doseModificationRules.text: Review required. Protocol-specific delay/reduce criteria may apply; physician decides.

drugs.name: OXALIplatin
drugs.notes: Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed., line 123719 (FOLFOX-6, Tournigand et al., 2004): oxaliplatin 100 mg/m2 over 2 hr, day 1 only, given concurrently with leucovorin. Cycle repeated every 14 d.

drugs.name: LEVOleucovorin
drugs.route: IV, concurrently with oxaliplatin (same line via Y-connector)
drugs.notes: Source line 123723: LV 400 mg/m2 concurrently with oxaliplatin, day 1 only.

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (bolus)
drugs.notes: Source line 123724: 5-FU bolus 400 mg/m2, day 1, given after the oxaliplatin/LV infusion (appendix F 'followed by' sequence).

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (continuous infusion)
drugs.notes: Source line 123725: 5-FU 1,200 mg/m2/d times 2 d (2,400 mg/m2 total infusion over 46-48 hr), following the bolus dose. dosePerUnit is the printed per-day rate (1,200 mg/m2/d); total course dose is 2,400 mg/m2 over the 2-day infusion.
